name: Benzylpenicillin
route_note: IV or IM injection; acid-labile, so not given orally (phenoxymethylpenicillin is the oral form). Long-acting benzathine and procaine salts are separate IM products.
originator: Alexander Fleming (St Mary's Hospital); developed by Howard Florey, Ernst Chain and colleagues (University of Oxford)

discovery.note: Observed that a Penicillium mould contaminating a staphylococcal culture plate killed the surrounding bacteria.

tagline: The original penicillin: an injectable beta-lactam that launched the antibiotic era
summary: Benzylpenicillin (penicillin G) is the natural penicillin first purified at Oxford in 1940 and mass-produced during the Second World War. It remains a first-choice injectable agent for streptococcal infections, syphilis, meningococcal disease and other infections caused by susceptible organisms.
mechanism: Benzylpenicillin acylates the active-site serine of penicillin-binding proteins, the transpeptidases that cross-link peptidoglycan strands in the bacterial cell wall. Inhibition of cross-linking weakens the wall and, together with dysregulated autolysins, leads to lysis of growing bacteria (bactericidal action).

It is hydrolysed by most beta-lactamases, including the staphylococcal penicillinase that became widespread from the 1950s, and penetrates the outer membrane of most Gram-negative bacilli poorly, which limits its spectrum to mainly Gram-positive bacteria, Neisseria, spirochaetes and some anaerobes.
uses: Diphtheria, anthrax, leptospirosis, actinomycosis and clostridial infections
Rheumatic fever and group B streptococcal intrapartum prophylaxis

history.title: Fleming's observation
history.detail: Alexander Fleming notes antibacterial activity of a Penicillium mould at St Mary's Hospital, London; published in 1929.

history.title: Oxford purification
history.detail: Florey, Chain, Heatley and colleagues purify penicillin and show it protects mice from streptococcal infection.

history.title: First patient
history.detail: Police constable Albert Alexander is treated in Oxford; he improves but dies when supplies run out.

history.title: Mass production
history.detail: US deep-tank fermentation, corn-steep liquor and higher-yielding Penicillium chrysogenum strains enable large-scale production for the Allied war effort.

history.title: Nobel Prize
history.detail: Fleming, Florey and Chain share the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine; Dorothy Hodgkin's X-ray crystallography confirms the beta-lactam structure around the same time.

history.title: Total synthesis
history.detail: John Sheehan at MIT reports the total synthesis of penicillin V.

history.title: 6-APA isolated
history.detail: Beecham researchers isolate the penicillin nucleus 6-aminopenicillanic acid, opening the way to semi-synthetic penicillins.

pk.excretion: renal, mainly by tubular secretion (blocked by probenecid)

serious: Seizures at very high doses or in renal failure

facts: Fleming, Florey and Chain shared the 1945 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for the discovery of penicillin and its curative effect.
Doses of benzylpenicillin are often expressed in units as well as milligrams, a legacy of early biological standardisation.
Penicillin was so scarce in the early 1940s that it was recovered from patients' urine for reuse.
